sections.overview: The common cuckoo is a migratory Eurasian bird best known for laying eggs in other birds’ nests.
sections.identification: Adults are slim, long-tailed birds with pointed wings; many have grey upperparts and finely barred pale underparts.
sections.habitat: It uses woodland edges, scrub and open country where suitable host birds and insect prey are available.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on insects, including caterpillars that many birds avoid because of their hairs.
sections.behavior: The male gives the familiar repeated ‘cuck-oo’ call; females are quieter and more elusive.
sections.reproduction: A female lays in the nest of a host species, which incubates the egg and feeds the chick; host choice varies among regions.
sections.ecology: Its breeding depends on host birds, while its insect diet links it to seasonal caterpillar populations.
sections.conservation: BTO reports a decline in the British population, with marked regional variation; that trend should not be generalized to the whole range.
